confirmation.description:
Confirmation must equal the datasource's name. Same defensive
shape the close-org dialog uses: it doesn't gate anything new
(the JWT + middleware already authorise the action) but stops
a curl-typo from wiping a live datasource and all its backup
history.

enabled.description:
Enabled toggles the scheduler gate for this one attachment. The
scheduler only enqueues jobs where attachment.enabled = true, so
setting this to false pauses just this policy on this data source
without losing schedule history or detaching the policy.

priority.description:
Priority orders concurrent attachments when multiple policies are
eligible to run on the same data source at the same minute.

isActive.description:
IsActive flips the master switch: false halts every backup policy
attached to this data source (the scheduler skips data sources with
is_active=false). Other fields above are simple metadata edits.

errorCode.description:
ErrorCode enum: not_found, not_succeeded, missing_artifact,
customer_managed_storage, presign_failed.

ok.description:
OK=true means url is a working presigned URL the client can
open directly. OK=false carries a structured ErrorCode +
ErrorMessage explaining why (job not finished, customer-
managed bucket, etc.); the response is still HTTP 200 so the
frontend can render the domain failure without hitting the
generic-transport-error path.

verifyOk.description:
Post-setup connection test (non-fatal — the setup is created either
way; verifyOk=false means the credentials need fixing before the
first backup will connect).

scratchConnectionString.description:
ScratchConnectionString is stored (KMS-enveloped) for a
customer_scratch target; empty leaves any existing creds in place.

policyId.description:
PolicyID is optional. Empty means "pick the highest-priority
enabled attachment on this datasource". Send a value when the
dialog's selector is changed away from the preselected one.

detectedVersion.description:
DetectedVersion is the server version read during the probe (e.g.
"17.4"), empty if the connection failed before it could be read.
DetectedVersionMajor is its major (17) — 0 if unknown. When the
major is outside what our dump tools support, ok is false and
errorCode is server_version_unsupported.

errorCode.description:
ErrorCode is empty on success; otherwise one of:
no_credentials, decrypt_failed, unsupported_engine, invalid_uri,
network_unreachable, auth_failed, timeout,
server_version_unsupported, unknown. Stable enum so the frontend
can branch without parsing text.

errorMessage.description:
ErrorMessage is a sanitised, human-readable explanation. Never
includes the connection string or credentials.

reachabilityOnly.description:
ReachabilityOnly = true means the probe confirmed the host is
reachable but didn't verify authentication. Reserved for a future
fast-path probe; both engines do full auth-aware pings today.

jobDeletedAt.description:
Soft-deletion fields populated by the retention worker. JobDeletedAt
is the wall-clock when the worker expired this backup; JobExpirationReason
is one of "age_exceeded" | "keep_last_n_exceeded".

verifyRestoreJobId.description:
VerifyRestoreJobID / VerifyHasLog point at the latest restore test's
job + whether its log is uploaded, so the row can open that log directly.

verifyStatus.description:
Latest restore-check of this backup. All null when it was never
verified. VerifyStatus is the verification restore's lifecycle status
(queued/running/success/failed); VerifyPassed is the pass/fail of the
validation ladder, meaningful once VerifyStatus is success; VerifiedAt
is when the check finished.

verifyWarnings.description:
VerifyWarnings is set when the restore test passed but pg_restore skipped
some objects (e.g. an index too large to rebuild) — "passed with warnings".
verifyWarnings.example: 1 object(s) could not be restored; e.g. index row size exceeds btree maximum

destinationId.description:
DestinationID — the storage_destination the policy writes to.
Required (NOT NULL on the table); every policy now declares
its destination at create time.

detectedEngineVersion.description:
DetectedEngineVersion is the server version read at the last
successful verify (e.g. "17.4"), omitted if never verified.
DetectedEngineVersionAt is when it was read.

restoreCheckTotal.description:
Restore-check health for the datasource-list health bar, aggregated
over the last few terminal verification checks. RestoreCheckTotal = 0
(or null) means the datasource has no checks yet. Present on list rows,
omitted on the by-ID detail read (which uses the health endpoint).

restoreCheckWarnings.description:
RestoreCheckWarnings is how many of the passed checks passed with
warnings (data restored but some object skipped) — drawn amber.

restoreTestingEnabled.description:
RestoreTestingEnabled is true when automated restore testing is on for
this datasource (config enabled and a cadence other than "off"). Present
on the by-ID detail read; omitted on list rows.

totalBackupJobs.description:
TotalBackupJobs counts every backup_job for this datasource
(any status, including retention-expired). Used by the FE
SectionCard count badge — the loaded-page count was misleading
for any datasource with more rows than fit on one page.

totalStoredBytes.description:
TotalStoredBytes is the total size still persisted in object
storage across every live backup for this datasource (excludes
retention-deleted backups). Only present on the by-ID detail read.

hasWebhookSecret.description:
HasWebhookSecret reports whether a signing secret is stored for the
webhook (the secret itself is never returned).

warnings.description:
Warnings is true when the check passed but skipped some object
(passed with warnings) — drawn amber in the status strip.

hasLog.description:
HasLog is true once the agent uploaded the restore output — the
logs.presign endpoint will return a link.

targetConnectionRef.description:
TargetConnectionRef is the redacted display form of the restore
target (scheme://…@host:port/db) — never carries credentials.

verifyPassed.description:
Verification fields — set only for verification checks
(trigger=verification). VerifyPassed is the validation-ladder outcome
(null until terminal); VerifyLevel is the depth reached (l1/l2/l3).

verifyWarnings.description:
VerifyWarnings is set when the restore passed but skipped some objects
(passed with warnings); null for a clean pass.
verifyWarnings.example: 1 object(s) could not be restored (see the restore log)

destinationId.description:
DestinationID is required: every policy now declares where its
archives land (migration 20260520121030 moved the column from
the attachment row to the policy itself). Customers picking
"this template uses my R2 bucket" once is cleaner than
re-picking on every datasource attach.

confirmOverwrite.description:
ConfirmOverwrite must be true for overwrite mode — the API guard
behind the wizard's confirm step.

mode.description: Mode is one of new_database | overwrite | new_server.

targetDatabase.description: TargetDatabase is the database to create (new_database mode only).

targetUri.description:
TargetURI is the write-capable connection string for new_database /
new_server modes. Encrypted at rest; never returned by any endpoint.

errorCode.description: ErrorCode is one of: not_found | no_log | presign_failed.

mode.description: Mode is one of new_database | overwrite | new_server.

targetDatabase.description: TargetDatabase (new_database mode) is probed for prior existence.

targetUri.description:
TargetURI is required for new_database / new_server; ignored for
overwrite (which probes the stored datasource credentials).

errorCode.description:
ErrorCode mirrors the verify enum plus write-probe codes:
target_not_writable | cannot_create_database | database_already_exists | engine_mismatch | …

get.description: Returns audit_log rows for the calling organization, newest first. Cursor-paginated via (createdAt, id) — pass nextCursorCreatedAt + nextCursorId from a response into the next request's cursorCreatedAt + cursorId to fetch the following page. Actor identity is resolved at read time via auth.BatchGetUsers; rows whose account has been anonymised (right-to-erasure) return empty actorEmail + actorName.

parameters.name: cursorCreatedAt

parameters.description: Cursor from prior response — UUID tiebreaker for same-timestamp rows
parameters.name: cursorId

parameters.description: Filter to rows with createdAt >= since (RFC3339)
parameters.name: since

parameters.description: Filter to rows with createdAt < until (RFC3339)
parameters.name: until

parameters.description: Filter to one or more exact actions (repeated)
parameters.name: actions

parameters.description: Filter by one or more exact target_types (repeated)
parameters.name: targetTypes

parameters.description: Filter by exact target uuid (e.g. one datasource's id)
parameters.name: targetId

parameters.description: Filter by one or more actor user ids (repeated)
parameters.name: actorIds

get.description: Returns every distinct user who has ever written an audit row for the calling organization, resolved via auth.BatchGetUsers. Anonymised accounts come back with empty email/name. Used to populate the audit-log Actor filter dropdown.
List all backup policies for the organization.

post.description: Create a new backup policy for the organization.

patch.description: Partially update a backup policy. Omitted fields are left unchanged.

get.description: Cross-datasource listing of backup jobs in the calling user's organization, sorted by created_at descending. Pass datasourceIds[] to filter to a subset of data sources. Org scoping is enforced at the SQL level — datasource ids belonging to other organizations are silently ignored.
Retrieve a paginated list of data sources for the organization.

parameters.description: Search query to filter data sources by name
parameters.name: query

post.description: Create a new data source for the organization.

Atomically creates a datasource + credentials + a default backup policy on a Norcube-managed destination and attaches it, so a new user gets a working scheduled backup from a single call. A failure at any step rolls everything back. After committing it runs a connection test and returns the result (non-fatal) so the caller can tell the user whether the first backup will connect.

get.description: Daily buckets of a data source's successful backups over the last N days (oldest → newest), for the storage-size and duration trend charts.
Retrieve a paginated list of backup jobs for the organization, with optional filtering by data source IDs.

post.description: Enqueues a manual backup_job row (trigger=manual) and returns its id. The 5-second Tick worker picks it up and launches a Fargate task. PolicyID is optional — leave empty to use the highest-priority enabled attachment for this datasource. Multiple concurrent runs of the same datasource + same policy are allowed by design (user explicitly clicked); the Fargate worker tolerates parallel jobs. Audit row backup_job.manual_run carries which policy was chosen and whether it was an explicit pick or the default.
post.summary: Run an ad-hoc backup of a datasource

delete.description: Hard-deletes the backup_job + cascades backup_artifact, removes the backup_retention_audit_log row (RESTRICT FK), and enqueues every (bucket, s3_key) pair for managed-S3 cleanup. Refuses with 409 if the job is currently `queued` or `running` (would race the Fargate worker). Writes one audit_log row with action `backup_job.deleted` before any destructive work. Customer-managed buckets are unaffected — we have no IAM on them, the DB row goes but the S3 file is the customer's responsibility.

post.description: Returns a presigned S3 GET URL for the backup archive (15-minute expiry). Both backup engines write exactly one archive per job (mongodump --archive piped through gzip; pg_dump --format=custom piped through gzip), so the response is a single URL — no per-artifact list. The handler is gated by MiddlewareDataSourceAccess + the SQL query filters on (org_id, data_source_id, job_id) for defence in depth. Every mint writes one audit_log row with action backup_job.download_link_generated. Customer-managed storage destinations return errorCode=customer_managed_storage because snapdb has no IAM on those buckets.
post.summary: Generate a download link for a backup file

post.description: Enqueue an on-demand verification restore of a backup into the datasource's configured scratch target. Recorded as a restore with trigger=verification, feeding the Restore health card.

get.description: List all policies attached to a specific data source.

post.description: Attach a backup policy to a data source with a specific storage destination.

delete.description: Detach a backup policy from a specific data source.

patch.description: Partial update of the join row between a data source and a backup policy. Setting `enabled=false` pauses that specific policy on that specific data source (the scheduler stops considering it) without detaching it — schedule history, jitter, and the cron expression are preserved. Use this when you want to temporarily silence one policy; use DELETE to remove the attachment entirely.

requestBody.description: Fields to patch (omit fields you don't want to change)

get.description: Recent terminal restore-checks (verification restores) of a data source, oldest → newest, for the Restore-health card's status strip and pass-rate.
Restore jobs for one datasource, newest first, cursor-paginated. Org + datasource scoping is enforced at the SQL level (and by the datasource-access middleware on the route).

parameters.description:
Trigger scopes the list: "manual" (user-initiated restore jobs,
default) or "verification" (automated/on-demand restore checks).
parameters.name: trigger

delete.description: Hard-deletes the data_sources row plus every backup_job, restore_job, pitr_timeline, and per-datasource policy attachment. Managed-S3 artifacts are enqueued into pending_s3_cleanup and dropped asynchronously by the s3sweep worker — they may take up to a minute to disappear from the bucket. Org-scoped policies and storage destinations are NOT removed (they're templates shared across other datasources). The request body must include a `confirmation` field whose value exactly matches the datasource's name, mirroring the close-org dialog's defensive shape. Refuses to run when a backup_job for this datasource is currently queued or running.

404.description: datasource not found in this org

409.description: in-flight backup job — wait or fail it first

delete.summary: Delete a datasource and all its backup history

get.description: Retrieve details of a specific data source by its ID.

patch.description: Partial update of a data source's metadata. Any field omitted is left unchanged. Set `isActive=false` to halt every backup policy attached to this data source without detaching them.

requestBody.description: Fields to patch (omit fields you don't want to change)

put.description: Set or update the credentials for a specific data source. Supports two types of credentials: username/password and connection URI.
put.summary: Set credentials for a data source

get.description: The datasource's automated restore-check configuration (an "off" default when never configured).

put.description: Create or update the datasource's automated restore-check configuration.

post.description: Decrypts the stored credential cipher in-process via KMS + AES-256-GCM and runs an engine-specific connectivity probe with a 5-second timeout. Postgres uses pgx.ConnectConfig + Ping; MongoDB uses the official driver's Ping(Primary) — both are real authentication checks. On success the probe also reads the server version (`detectedVersion`/`detectedVersionMajor`) and, if it's newer than the bundled dump tools support, returns ok=false with errorCode `server_version_unsupported` so an unsupported server is caught at connect time rather than at backup time. Never returns the connection string or any credential material in the response or audit log.
post.summary: Test the connection for a datasource

get.description: The org's failure-alerting configuration. Defaults (all alert types on, email to org members) when never configured.

put.description: Create or update the org's failure-alerting configuration. webhookSecret is write-only: omitted keeps the stored secret; clearing webhookUrl drops it.

post.description: Push a synthetic alert through every configured channel (email, Slack, webhook) and report per-channel results.

Creates a restore job from a successful backup and dispatches it to a restore worker. Modes: `new_database` (create a fresh DB on a server you point at — targetUri needs create-database rights, targetDatabase is the name to create), `overwrite` (restore over the datasource's existing database using its stored credentials — requires confirmOverwrite=true and a write-capable role), `new_server` (restore into the database named in targetUri). Probe the target first via POST /restores/target-probe. Restores are deliberately not billing-gated.

The restore wizard's pre-flight. For `overwrite` it checks the datasource's stored credentials can actually write (creates + drops a throwaway norcube_write_test table/collection) — backup roles are usually read-only, so this catches the failure before anything runs. For `new_database` it checks the supplied targetUri can create databases and that targetDatabase doesn't exist yet; for `new_server` it write-probes the database named in targetUri. Domain failures come back as errorCode/errorMessage with HTTP 200.
post.summary: Probe a restore target for writability

get.description: Full detail of a restore job, including status, byte counters, the redacted target, and whether a log is available.

Returns a short-lived presigned URL for the restore run's output log (the redacted pg_restore / mongorestore output the worker uploaded). Available for both successful and failed restores once the worker has reported; `errorCode: no_log` until then.
get.summary: Get a link to the restore's log

get.description: Returns every storage destination an organization can attach to a backup policy — both Norcube-managed buckets and BYO (customer-owned) S3-compatible destinations. Credential fields are never included in the response; the agent dispatcher fetches them via a separate decrypt path when starting a job. Supports server-side filtering by search substring (matched against name / bucket / endpoint / type), ownership (`all` / `managed` / `byo`), and unverifiedOnly (BYO rows whose verify rotted).

parameters.description: Substring search across name, bucket, endpoint URL, and type
parameters.name: search

parameters.description: Filter by ownership: all | managed | byo
parameters.name: ownership

parameters.description: Only return BYO rows with NULL last_verified_at
parameters.name: unverifiedOnly

post.description: Registers a customer-owned S3-compatible storage destination (AWS S3 outside our account, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, MinIO, etc.). The supplied credentials are verified end-to-end (PutObject → HeadObject → DeleteObject of a tiny probe object) BEFORE the row is persisted — if any step fails the request returns 400 and nothing is saved. Credentials are KMS-wrapped (envelope-encrypted with the same {org_id, destination_id} context we use for datasource credentials) before persistence and never leave the encrypted path again until the agent dispatcher unseals them at job-start time.
Ensure that a managed storage destination exists for the given region. If it does not exist, it will be created.

delete.description: Soft-deletes a customer-owned (BYO) storage destination (sets is_active=false and wipes the credential blob). Refuses with 409 if any data_source_policy still references this destination — the customer must detach those policies first. Managed destinations cannot be deleted through this endpoint.

get.description: Returns a single storage destination by id, scoped to the calling organization.

patch.description: Updates a customer-owned (BYO) storage destination. Two paths: metadata-only (name / storageClass / encryptionMode) writes immediately. Any connection-knob change (region / endpointUrl / forcePathStyle) OR credential change requires accessKeyId + secretAccessKey to be supplied together — the new combination is re-verified end-to-end (PutObject → HeadObject → DeleteObject) before the row is updated. Managed destinations cannot be edited through this endpoint.
